entries.3cd4d335ae0c3620: It is a company that originated in painting, and it has no parent or subsidiary companies and reports on a standalone basis. With the mission 'Clean, Toward the Future', it deploys two technologies, SOSEI and CoolLaser, to keep aging factories and infrastructure such as bridges and steel towers in good condition over the long term. The securities report designates these two as reportable [[term:segment|segments]].

entries.5f3ebeec4528caa2: This business develops, manufactures and sells the “CoolLaser” system, which removes rust and old paint film using high-output laser light, and also carries out construction work on bridges, steel towers and other structures. Its strength is that, unlike blasting methods, it produces no industrial waste such as abrasive materials. Revenue consists of sales of equipment sold for around ¥100 million, sales of consumables such as protective lenses, maintenance revenue from maintenance contracts, and construction revenue, mainly from trial construction work. The company wants the CoolLaser method to be used not only by itself but also by infrastructure owners and construction companies nationwide; it does not actively grow construction revenue and aims to grow through equipment sales and recurring revenue, such as maintenance contracts and consumables sales after equipment is delivered. For the fiscal year ended March 2026, revenue was ¥1,350 million (up 219.3% year on year) and segment profit was ¥249 million (compared with a segment loss of ¥69 million in the prior-year period). The company explains that it delivered 12 units over the full year and that cases of a single company introducing multiple units and repeat orders have also emerged.

entries.771dc7ab44fafeb6: This is a business that carries out reinforcement work (SOSEI method) by spraying a special fast-curing resin onto the aging slate roofs of factories and other buildings. It is a method independently developed by the company in 2006; by March 2026, it had a cumulative record of 1.7 million m² of construction, mainly repairing factories of automobile and electrical equipment manufacturers. Beyond developing the method, the company continues “responsible construction,” in which one of its own construction managers is permanently stationed at each site and the work is carried out under the company's own responsibility. Depending on the case, the company receives orders directly from the client, or it works as a subcontractor when another construction company is the prime contractor; spraying work is outsourced to partner contractors. For the fiscal year ended March 2026, revenue was ¥1,783 million (up 11.3% year on year) and segment profit was ¥630 million (up 10.2% year on year). Large renovation projects at domestic factories in the automotive, machinery and steel industries led to higher revenue.
entries.7747aee761b945bf: In roof reinforcement work (SOSEI Business), it receives construction payments from the party placing the order.
entries.8106927b552b959a: Sales of equipment and consumables in CoolLaser Business
entries.84cab2a85d93df74: The SOSEI method reinforces aging roofs by spraying a special instantly curing resin onto them; once the second layer is applied, the roof is strong enough for workers to stand on without breaking through, and the first layer of urethane foam lowers the roof-space temperature in summer by up to about 20°C. Under a contract, the second-layer material (SOSEI coat) is mainly purchased in its entirety from Mitsubishi Chemical Infratech Corporation. CoolLaser is a device that uses a high-output laser to remove rust and coatings, and its strength is that it produces no industrial waste such as abrasive materials. The company cites a high output of 5.4 kW and long-distance transmission of up to 100 m through optical fiber cable as features. For the equipment, the laser heads are assembled by the company, the other components are assembled at contract manufacturers' plants, and the company joins them together before shipment to verify performance.

entries.cdd9968fadf8b13f: Revenue for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥3,133 million (up 54.7% year on year). SOSEI Business revenue was ¥1,783 million (up 11.3% year on year), increasing due to large renovation projects at domestic factories in industries such as automotive, machinery, and steel. CoolLaser Business revenue was ¥1,350 million (up 219.3% year on year), with 12 units delivered over the full year. In the revenue recognition note of the securities report, most CoolLaser Business revenue is classified as 'sale of goods and products'. The securities report states that the company does not actively expand construction revenue, and aims to grow through equipment sales and recurring revenue such as maintenance contracts and consumables sales after equipment delivery.

entries.d8fc25a791715e08: Operating profit for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥629 million (up 108.8% year on year), ordinary profit was ¥618 million (up 135.4%), and net income was ¥550 million (up 71.4%). Segment profit was ¥630 million for SOSEI Business (up 10.2% year on year), and ¥249 million for CoolLaser Business (the prior-year period recorded a segment loss of ¥69 million). Operating profit is segment profit less corporate expenses not allocated to reportable segments. The securities report cites revenue, operating profit, and order backlog as indicators for judging the achievement of management targets.
